name: Gad
overview: Gad is a male figure in the Bible, known as the seventh-born son of Jacob through Zilpah, Leah's handmaid. He is the progenitor of the tribe of Gad, one of the tribes of Israel. His identity is closely tied to his lineage and tribal affiliation.
namesAndTitles: The name Gad means 'fortune' and is a proper name given by Jacob rather than directly by God. This name reflects a sense of blessing or good fortune associated with his birth.
familyAndRelationships: Gad is explicitly identified as the son of Jacob and Zilpah. He has numerous half-brothers including Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, Issachar, Zebulun, Joseph, and Benjamin, as well as a brother named Asher. His familial connections extend to many of the patriarchs of Israel, situating him within the broader family of Jacob's sons.
scriptureSignificance: Gad's significance in Scripture lies in his role as the ancestor of the tribe of Gad, which became known for its warrior character and faithfulness to Israel. The tribe settled east of the Jordan River in fertile pasturelands, contributing to the strength and diversity of the Israelite nation. His birth and name symbolize a divine blessing of fortune and military strength that shaped the tribe's identity.
